title: Niger–Congo languages - Wikipedia
text: Niger–Congo is a proposed family of African languages spoken over the majority of sub-Saharan Africa. It unites the Mande languages, the Atlantic–Congo languages, and possibly several smaller groups of languages that are difficult to classify.

title: Lafofa languages ::: Open WIKI
text: Lafofa, also Tegem–Amira, is a Niger–Congo dialect cluster spoken in the southern Nuba Mountains in the south of Sudan. Blench considers the Tegem and Amira varieties to be distinct languages; as Lafofa is poorly attested, there may be others.

text: The classification of Kordofanian languages within the Niger-Congo family has been the subject of considerable scholarly debate. Kordofanian languages are typically divided into five branches: Heiban, Koalib, Talodi–Heiban, Rashad, and Katla–Tima (also known as Lafofa–Tima).
